decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2 to 2-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed lowered interest rates due to global economic uncertainty and low inflation.

changes.quote: The Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings in the System Open Market Account in August, two months earlier than previously indicated.
changes.explanation: The Fed stopped shrinking its bond portfolio two months earlier than planned.

changes.quote: Although growth of household spending has picked up from earlier in the year, growth of business fixed investment has been soft.
changes.explanation: Consumer spending improved, but business investment weakened.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed.
changes.explanation: Market measures show inflation is still running below target.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.09% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.02% and moved -4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.81% would fall by about $6.83 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 181k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (June 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -1.09%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.11% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will continue watching incoming economic data to decide on future rate changes. As an educational note, the forecast model suggests a hold is most likely at the next meeting with a 78% probability.
